See the code: https://github.com/BrianS3/gas_forecasting/blob/main/R/gas_EDA.Rmd

All prices are the **U.S. national weekly average, all grades, dollars per gallon** from the
U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). Prices are not adjusted for inflation.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)
source(here("R", "gas_data_prep.R"))
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = "100%")

dollars <- function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2))

# --- headline numbers ---
latest       <- gas_weekly %>% slice_max(date, n = 1)
four_wks_ago <- gas_weekly %>% filter(date <= latest$date - 28) %>% slice_max(date, n = 1)
one_yr_ago   <- gas_weekly %>% filter(date <= latest$date - 364) %>% slice_max(date, n = 1)
record       <- gas_weekly %>% slice_max(price, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
this_year    <- gas_weekly %>% filter(year(date) == year(latest$date))
year_low     <- this_year %>% slice_min(price, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
year_high    <- this_year %>% slice_max(price, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

change_text <- function(now, then) {
  diff <- now - then
  paste0(ifelse(diff >= 0, "up ", "down "), dollars(abs(diff)),
         " (", percent(diff / then, accuracy = 1), ")")
}

# --- 2-month projection (written by gas_forecasting_process.R) ---
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), here("database", "gas_data.db"))
projection <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_two_month")
projection_monthly <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_monthly") %>%
  mutate(month = as.Date(month))
dbDisconnect(con)

# --- the first full week on/after each event, so we can put a dot on the line ---
events_on_chart <- key_events %>%
  left_join(gas_weekly %>% select(week = date, price, president),
            by = join_by(closest(date <= week))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(price))
```

# Where prices stand

| | |
|---|---|
| **Latest week** (`r format(latest$date, "%b %d, %Y")`) | **`r dollars(latest$price)`** per gallon |
| vs. 4 weeks ago | `r change_text(latest$price, four_wks_ago$price)` |
| vs. 1 year ago | `r change_text(latest$price, one_yr_ago$price)` |
| `r year(latest$date)` range so far | `r dollars(year_low$price)` (`r format(year_low$date, "%b %d")`) to `r dollars(year_high$price)` (`r format(year_high$date, "%b %d")`) |
| Record high | `r dollars(record$price)` (`r format(record$date, "%b %d, %Y")`) |
| **Projected average, `r format(as.Date(projection$start_month), "%b")`–`r format(as.Date(projection$end_month), "%b %Y")`** | **`r dollars(projection$projected)`** (likely range `r dollars(projection$lower_80)`–`r dollars(projection$upper_80)`). See [Gas Forecasting Results](gas_forecasting_results.html) |

# What's going on

*Written November 2026. Update this section by hand when the story changes.*

- **War with Iran pushed prices up fast.** The U.S. and Israel struck Iran on February 28, 2026, and Iran cut off
  access to the Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil. The national average went from
  `r dollars(filter(gas_monthly, month == as.Date("2026-01-01"))$price)` in January to
  `r dollars(filter(gas_monthly, month == as.Date("2026-05-01"))$price)` in May, the sharpest monthly run-up in the
  data, steeper than after Hurricane Katrina in 2005 or Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
- **A second crude spike in September.** Prices eased over the summer and then climbed again. EIA attributes the
  September increase to higher crude oil prices plus wider refining margins ("crack spreads").
- **What EIA expects next.** EIA's October 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook expects retail gasoline to hold near
  September levels in October and then slowly decrease along with crude oil prices.

Sources: [EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, Oct 2026](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/Oct26.pdf),
[PBS NewsHour](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/iran-war-hits-home-as-gasoline-prices-fuel-significant-u-s-inflation-jump),
[Kelley Blue Book / AAA](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/aaa-national-average-gas-prices-spiked-in-march-2026/).

```{r recent chart, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
recent_start <- latest$date - years(2)

recent_weeks  <- gas_weekly %>% filter(date >= recent_start)
recent_events <- events_on_chart %>% filter(date >= recent_start)

recent_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = recent_weeks,
            aes(x = date, y = price, group = 1,
                text = paste0("Week of ", format(date, "%b %d, %Y"), "<br>", dollars(price))),
            color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = projection_monthly,
             aes(x = month + 14, y = projected,
                 text = paste0(format(month, "%B %Y"), " projection<br>", dollars(projected),
                               " (", dollars(lower_80), "-", dollars(upper_80), ")")),
             color = "#2F855A", size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(data = projection_monthly,
                aes(x = month + 14, ymin = lower_80, ymax = upper_80),
                color = "#2F855A", width = 8) +
  geom_point(data = recent_events,
             aes(x = week, y = price, text = paste0(event, "<br>", format(date, "%b %d, %Y"))),
             color = "#D69E2E", size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b '%y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Last 2 years: weekly price (black), events (gold), 2-month projection (green)",
       x = "", y = "Dollars per gallon")

ggplotly(recent_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

# The long view: price and who was in charge

The top chart is the weekly national average since 1993. Shading shows the president's party
(**blue = Democrat, red = Republican**) and gold dots mark major events. The bottom strip shows which party
held the White House, Senate, and House. Hover for details, and drag to zoom (double-click to reset).

```{r timeline, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
first_week <- min(gas_weekly$date)
last_week  <- max(gas_weekly$date)
top        <- max(gas_weekly$price) * 1.1

# shading behind the price line, one band per presidential term
pres_bands <- presidencies %>%
  mutate(start = pmax(start, first_week), end = pmin(end, last_week),
         middle = start + (end - start) / 2)

price_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = pres_bands,
            aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = 0, ymax = top, fill = pres_party, text = label),
            alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_text(data = pres_bands, aes(x = middle, y = top * 0.97, label = president), size = 3) +
  geom_line(data = gas_weekly,
            aes(x = date, y = price, group = 1,
                text = paste0("Week of ", format(date, "%b %d, %Y"), "<br>", dollars(price),
                              "<br>President: ", president,
                              "<br>Senate: ", senate, " | House: ", house)),
            color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = events_on_chart,
             aes(x = week, y = price, text = paste0(event, "<br>", format(date, "%b %d, %Y"))),
             color = "#D69E2E", size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = party_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Dollars per gallon")

# strip showing party control of each branch
control_strip <- control_periods %>%
  filter(end > first_week) %>%
  mutate(start = pmax(start, first_week), end = pmin(end, last_week)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(pres_party, senate, house), names_to = "body", values_to = "party") %>%
  mutate(body = recode(body, pres_party = "White House", senate = "Senate", house = "House"),
         row  = match(body, c("House", "Senate", "White House")))

strip_plot <- ggplot(control_strip) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = row - 0.45, ymax = row + 0.45, fill = party,
                text = paste0(body, ": ", party, "<br>", format(start, "%b %Y"), " to ", format(end, "%b %Y"))),
            color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = party_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = c("House", "Senate", "White House")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")

subplot(ggplotly(price_plot, tooltip = "text"),
        ggplotly(strip_plot, tooltip = "text"),
        nrows = 2, heights = c(0.78, 0.22), shareX = TRUE, titleY = TRUE)
```

## By president

```{r by president}
by_president <- gas_weekly %>%
  mutate(term_id = consecutive_id(president)) %>%
  group_by(term_id, president, pres_party) %>%
  summarise(from        = min(date),
            to          = max(date),
            avg_price   = mean(price),
            first_price = first(price),
            last_price  = last(price),
            low         = min(price),
            high        = max(price),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(change = last_price - first_price)

by_president %>%
  transmute(President = president, Party = pres_party,
            From = format(from, "%b %Y"),
            To   = ifelse(to == last_week, "now", format(to, "%b %Y")),
            `Average` = dollars(avg_price),
            `Price at start` = dollars(first_price),
            `Price at end`   = dollars(last_price),
            `Change`         = paste0(ifelse(change >= 0, "+", "-"), dollars(abs(change))),
            `Low`  = dollars(low),
            `High` = dollars(high)) %>%
  kable(align = "llllrrrrrr")
```

*Clinton's row starts in April 1993, when EIA's weekly series begins.*

## By who controlled Washington

Each row is a stretch where the White House, Senate, and House majorities stayed the same.

```{r by control period}
by_control <- gas_weekly %>%
  mutate(period_id = consecutive_id(president, house, senate)) %>%
  group_by(period_id, president, pres_party, senate, house, control) %>%
  summarise(from        = min(date),
            to          = max(date),
            avg_price   = mean(price),
            first_price = first(price),
            last_price  = last(price),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(change = last_price - first_price)

by_control %>%
  transmute(From = format(from, "%b %Y"),
            To   = ifelse(to == last_week, "now", format(to, "%b %Y")),
            President = paste0(president, " (", pres_party, ")"),
            Senate = senate, House = house, Control = control,
            `Average` = dollars(avg_price),
            `Price at start` = dollars(first_price),
            `Price at end`   = dollars(last_price),
            `Change` = paste0(ifelse(change >= 0, "+", "-"), dollars(abs(change)))) %>%
  kable(align = "lllcccrrrr")
```

**Read these tables with care.** Gas prices mostly follow the global price of crude oil, which is driven by
wars, OPEC decisions, recessions, and hurricanes far more than by who holds office. Every big move on the
chart above lines up with one of those events. Prices have also risen over 30+ years with inflation,
so later administrations will tend to show higher averages regardless of policy.

# Patterns worth knowing

## Typical seasonal pattern

```{r seasonality, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
seasonal_years <- (year(Sys.Date()) - 15):(year(Sys.Date()) - 1)

seasonal <- gas_monthly %>%
  mutate(year = year(month), month_name = month(month, label = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(year %in% seasonal_years) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(vs_year_avg = price / mean(price) - 1) %>%
  group_by(month_name) %>%
  summarise(typical = median(vs_year_avg), .groups = "drop")

cheapest <- seasonal %>% slice_min(typical, n = 1)
priciest <- seasonal %>% slice_max(typical, n = 1)

seasonal_plot <- ggplot(seasonal, aes(x = month_name, y = typical,
                                      text = paste0(month_name, ": ", percent(typical, accuracy = 0.1),
                                                    " vs. that year's average"))) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = typical > 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#C05621", "FALSE" = "#2B6CB0")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = paste0("How each month compares to its year's average (median, ",
                      min(seasonal_years), "-", max(seasonal_years), ")"),
       x = "", y = "")

ggplotly(seasonal_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

Over the last 15 years, gas has typically been cheapest in **`r cheapest$month_name`**
(`r percent(cheapest$typical, accuracy = 0.1)` vs. the year's average) and most expensive in
**`r priciest$month_name`** (`r percent(priciest$typical, accuracy = 0.1)`). Prices usually climb in spring as
refiners switch to summer-blend gasoline and driving season starts, then ease into winter.

## Year by year

```{r yearly averages, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
yearly <- gas_weekly %>%
  mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(avg_price = mean(price),
            pres_party = names(which.max(table(pres_party))),   # party in office most of the year
            .groups = "drop")

yearly_plot <- ggplot(yearly, aes(x = year, y = avg_price, fill = pres_party,
                                  text = paste0(year, ifelse(year == year(last_week), " (so far)", ""),
                                                ": ", dollars(avg_price)))) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = party_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1993, year(last_week), by = 2)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Average price by year (bar color = president's party for most of the year)",
       x = "", y = "Dollars per gallon")

ggplotly(yearly_plot, tooltip = "text")
```
